messages:
Ethan W.: Hi team, first-day laptop question. Got a Lenovo ThinkPad with Ubuntu 22.04. I ran the initial setup and installed the Redwood Endpoint Agent, but enrollment failed saying 'LUKS key escrow blocked: secure boot enabled'. I haven't disabled secure boot before—do I need to? I'm remote and a bit nervous about that.
IT Help: Welcome Ethan 44b We support Linux devices but the LUKS escrow flow does require either secure boot to be disabled or using our signed shim so the agent can unlock and escrow keys at boot. Which BIOS/UEFI version do you have?
Ethan W.: BIOS shows: "Lenovo 1.45 07/15/2024". How would I get the signed shim?
enroll-bot: Enrollment attempt logged for asset TAG-LTP-7782 by ethan@redwood.ai 4dd policy: linux-luks-escrow triggered (ticket #MDM-2026-812).
Security Alex: Hey Ethan, you don't have to permanently disable secure boot. We provide a pre-signed shim (rwi-shim.efi) that you can register in MokList so the agent can access the TPM-backed LUKS key and escrow it safely. Steps are a bit hands-on but we'll walk you through.
DevEx Mia: I'm around to pair if you want. We'll do it over a Zoom and I can guide you through the UEFI UI if you're not comfy.
IT Help: Quick checklist: 1) Backup any important data. 2) Have your recovery USB ready. 3) We'll provide the signed shim and a one-time MOK enrollment token. If you'd rather we ship an image with shim preinstalled, let us know (takes 1-2 days).
Ethan W.: I'd like to do it today if possible. Pairing works. Also, how do I confirm secure boot currently status from Ubuntu?
IT Help: Run: `mokutil --sb-state` and paste the output here. Also `sudo cryptsetup status /dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-root` to show LUKS status (no passphrases).
Ethan W.: mokutil output: "SecureBoot enabled". cryptsetup: "/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-root: active, keyslots: 2".
Security Alex: Ok that matches. We'll generate the shim and MOK token. Ethan, can you open a temporary SSH port on your router or use the Zoom share for the MOK steps? We avoid SSH if you're on home NAT without port forwarding.
Ethan W.: Zoom screenshare is easiest. Ready in 10.
DevEx Mia: On call now. First step I'm uploading the shim to our CDN and creating MOK token (one-time).
IT Help: Paste this command when prompted on the machine to enroll the shim after we upload it: `sudo mokutil --import /tmp/rwi-shim.cer && sudo reboot` Then when the machine reboots you'll see the MOK manager UI to confirm the cert enrollment.
Security Alex: Note: after MOK enrollment the shim will be trusted, agent can access the TPM and escrow the LUKS key. We'll watch the enrollment logs on our side.
Ethan W.: Done import step, rebooting now. Seeing the blue MOK manager screen 4f0. Choosing "Enroll key from disk" and confirming.
enroll-bot: Remote action: shim cert enrolled for TAG-LTP-7782 by Security Alex (token 1Hf3-XL).
Ethan W.: Back up. Re-ran agent enrollment: agent shows "escrow successful" and the web console shows device as "Managed - LUKS escrowed".
IT Help: Great. Two follow-ups: 1) Run `sudo update-initramfs -u` to ensure shim persists across kernel updates. 2) We'll email you the recovery escrow ID (for support use only).
DevEx Mia: I'll drop a dotfiles/bootstrap script in your home that installs common dev tools without requiring root. If you need Docker, we use the rootless setup on Linux: https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/rootless/
Ethan W.: Thanks everyone! One more question: if I ever want to switch to a personal disk image, do I need to unenroll first?
Security Alex: Yes, unenroll and we will revoke the shim cert for that device. We'll provide steps; usually it's `sudo mokutil --delete` and then we clear the escrowed key from the console.
Ethan W.: Copy. File a quick note: enrollment ticket MDM-2026-812 looks good to close once you confirm key escrow retention policy.
IT Help: We'll keep the ticket open 24h to verify automatic unlock across one reboot cycle and kernel update. Marking as in-progress.
Ethan W.: Rebooted twice and LUKS unlock worked both times. Thanks for the in-call help, much appreciated 64f
